sources.entry: Garlic-Hub - Digital signage device and content management system with SMIL playlist support and scheduling. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: Garlic-Hub is a self-hosted digital signage management system for managing devices, media content and SMIL playlists from one web interface.
summary.what_it_does: Garlic-Hub manages signage devices, media and playlists through a single self-hosted web interface. Media can be organized in hierarchical folders and uploaded from local files, or added as external links, screencasts, camera or stock platforms (the latter with an API key). A graphical editor builds multi-zone layouts, and an image template editor based on fabric.js is included. Playlists can be exported in the SMIL format, with date and time conditions for playback and triggers that play media or nested playlists by priority (via access keys, touch/click, date/time or network). It can push a playlist to one local player. User management provides roles per module, session login with remember-me, basic OAuth2 token authorization, and a UI in English, German, Spanish, French, Greek and Russian.
use_cases: manage digital signage displays from a central place
schedule media playback by date and time
push playlists to a local media player
create SMIL playlists for signage players
how_to_run: git clone <repository URL> (not specified in the README)
cp .env.dist .env # then fill in the values
notable: Part of the GarlicSignage ecosystem, alongside garlic-player (SMIL media player), garlic-launcher (Android kiosk), garlic-daemon and garlic-proxy
Exports playlists in the industry-standard SMIL format
Trigger-based playback by priority from access keys, touch, schedule or network
Includes a threat model document and CycloneDX SBOM per release
Public live demo available, rebuilt regularly
caveats: Project is in active development, so code and APIs may still change
Setup requires PHP 8.4 with several extensions (including imagick) and recommends Docker with DDEV for local development
Push supports only one local player per the feature table; the README lists it as 'integration of one local media player'
